      Fixes: #15139
Two Appenders race when creating a series with a native histogram as the memSeries will be common and the lastHistogram field is written without lock.
Fix by:
Move writing memSeries lastHistogramValue and lastFloatHistogramValue
after series creation under lock.
The resulting code isn't totally correct in the sense that we're setting
these values before Commit() , so they might be overwritten/rolled back
later.
Also Append() of stale sample checks the values without lock, so there's
still a potential race.
The correct solution would be to set these only in Commit() which we
actually do, but then Commit() would also need to process samples in
order and not floats first, then histograms, then float histograms - which
leads to not knowing what stale marker to write for histograms.
Might be easier to do after : #15112

part.text:
Fixed. The race in `tsdb.headAppender.AppendHistogram` occurred because `memSeries.lastHistogramValue`/`lastFloatHistogramValue` were written without holding the series lock when a new series was created, while `Commit` writes the same fields under the lock from a concurrent appender.

Applied the upstream fix (krajorama's PR #15142, commit bb70370) to `tsdb/head_append.go`:
- Refactored `headAppender.getOrCreate` to return `created`
- Moved the `lastHistogramValue`/`lastFloatHistogramValue` initialization out of the unlocked creation path into the existing `s.Lock()` sections of `AppendHistogram`, `AppendHistogramCTZeroSample`

Verification:
- `go build ./tsdb/` passes
- `go test -race -run "TestHeadAppendHistogramAndCommitConcurrency|TestAppendHistogram"` passes (no data race)
- `go test -race -run "TestAppend|TestHeadAppend|TestCommit" ./tsdb/` passes
- Full `go test ./tsdb/`: only failure is `TestDelayedCompaction`, which also fails on the pristine tree (pre-existing, unrelated to this change)
